GS.rationale: Goldman Sachs has a genuinely elite franchise (#1 global M&A, record Q1 2026 results with $17.23B revenue and $17.55 EPS, +24% YoY EPS growth) and a credible strategic pivot toward fee-based AWM revenue. The SpaceX IPO lead-underwriter role and record $560M in fees demonstrate continued dominance in marquee capital-markets events. However, the stock has already re-rated aggressively: P/E of 18.7x and P/B of 2.75x are both at the absolute top of their 365-day ranges, with only ~84bps earnings yield spread over 10Y Treasuries. The balance sheet is levering (16.8x assets/equity vs 14.5x two quarters prior), and TTM data is incomplete (Q4 2025 missing), preventing validation of full-cycle sustainability. Q2 2026 earnings (July 14) could serve as a near-term catalyst but faces a tough sequential comparison against Q1's record, with consensus expecting ~$13.76-13.84 EPS and ~$15.8B revenue — a meaningful step-down. The fundamental trajectory is positive but the valuation has fully caught up, leaving asymmetric downside risk at these multiples. Score reflects a strong franchise at fair-to-full valuation with limited upside withoutation, tempered by the upcoming earnings event.
